title: The Blue Jackal
text:
A hungry jackal named Chandarava wandered into a town looking for food. The town dogs chased him, and in his panic he leapt into a large vat of indigo dye in a dyer's yard. When he crawled out and escaped into the forest, his fur was a deep, strange blue.

The forest animals had never seen anything like him. Lions, tigers, elephants and leopards all drew back in fear. The jackal saw his chance. He announced that the creator had made him in this unusual color and sent him to be king of the beasts. The animals believed him and served him. He made the lion his minister, the tiger his chamberlain, and gave other high posts to the great animals. His own kind, the jackals, he drove out in contempt so no one would recognize him.

One evening a pack of jackals began to howl in the distance. Chandarava's nature was stronger than his disguise. Without thinking, he threw back his head and howled in answer. The lion and the tiger looked at each other, understood that their king was only a jackal, and tore him to pieces.
lesson: Authority built on an image, rather than on who you really are, lasts only until a moment of pressure reveals you. It is safer to lead as yourself and to stay loyal to the people you came from.
people: Chandarava the jackal, the forest animals
